title: Goal environment
description: environments/<name>.yaml in a factory definition (ADR 0037 decision 5): what an agent's box installs and what it can reach. Its name is its file name; every factory has environments/default.yaml, which an agent without an environment gets. A {{secret}} reference names an organization secret and is valid only in env, files and mcp (headers, and a stdio server's env).

name.description: The file name without .yaml; written for readers, and must match it when present.

description.description: What the environment is for, in one sentence.

size.description: How much CPU and memory the box gets; medium when omitted.

image.description: The box's container image; Goal's agent image when omitted.

tools.description: mise tool specs (go@1.26, npm:@acme/cli@2) the box installs after the repository's own mise.toml or .tool-versions.

setup.description: Commands run in order after the clone and the tools. Each must finish in 30 minutes; a non-zero exit fails the run.

env.description: Variables the box gets, by name: a plain value, or one with {{secret}} references as the whole value or part of it (postgres://app:{{db-pass}}@db/app). Names the platform keeps (GOAL_*, HOME, PATH…) are refused at publish.

files.description: Files written before setup with mode 0600, by path: an absolute path or one that starts with ~/. Each value is a {{secret}} reference.

mcp.description: MCP servers the agent gets, by name (a slug, as environment tests and standing rules name it): each is remote (url, optional headers) or stdio (command, optional env), never both.

reference.description: A whole {{secret}} reference: the name of an organization secret open to the factory.

headers.description: Remote: the headers of every request, with {{secret}} references, such as Authorization: Bearer {{linear-key}}.

command.description: Stdio: the command and its arguments, run in the box.

env.description: Stdio: the server's own variables, with {{secret}} references.

tools.description: Tool modes by tool name or glob (delete_*): allow, ask or off. The most specific match wins; a tool nothing matches is allow.
